record.title: A preprint reports GPT-6 Astra leading a simulated robot benchmark, with sharp control limits
record.summary: A September 21, 2026 arXiv preprint reports an evaluation of GPT-6 Astra acting directly as a robot manipulation policy, without task-specific fine-tuning or a learned motor policy in the control path. Across 42 RoboDojo simulation tasks and 2,100 trials, the authors report 22.48% average success and a score of 28.97, above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven: Astra trails the top policy on precision, long-horizon and memory axes, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash perform much worse in the same reported interface. The authors say they stopped real-robot trials after unsafe actions damaged equipment; the paper does not establish real-world reliability or safe control. These are preprint-reported results without independent reproduction, and the public-policy runs did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs.

claims.label: DEMONSTRATED
claims.text: The arXiv v1 preprint exists and describes an evaluation of a frozen GPT-6 Astra model selecting robot end-effector targets directly, with non-learned target validation/path conversion and no learned policy in the control path.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that GPT-6 Astra achieved 22.48% micro average success and 28.97 score over 2,100 RoboDojo simulation trials across 42 tasks, ranking above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven, and public-policy comparisons did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: The authors report that they halted real-robot testing after physically unreasonable or unsafe actions damaged hardware; they report no person was injured. These are statements in the preprint, not independently verified incident findings.

claims.label: CLAIMED
claims.text: On selected perturbation trials, the authors report continued task success under some altered visual/action conditions and describe traces consistent with within-episode correction; the small probes do not isolate the feedback mechanism or establish general adaptation.

evidence_gaps.description: No independent reproduction of the 42-task simulation results or audit of episode-level records was recovered.
Compared public policies and the LLMs were not given identical task information: the paper says LLMs received wiki-derived task recipes while public-policy runs did not.
The paper says real-robot trials stopped after unsafe actions damaged equipment; the event and any real-world reliability claims were not independently corroborated.

brief.importance_rationale: If the bounded benchmark result generalizes under matched information and is reproduced, a general language model could perform useful robot manipulation without a task-specific learned motor policy, affecting robotics system design. The current evidence is one unreproduced preprint with low absolute success, uneven task performance, non-identical information for the compared systems and an author-reported unsafe hardware boundary, so this is consequential but not field-shifting.
limitations: Single unreproduced preprint; reported outcomes are author claims, not independently demonstrated results.
RoboDojo is a simulation benchmark; the authors say hardware testing was halted after unsafe actions and equipment damage. Safe or reliable real-world robot control is not established.
The model has low absolute success and sharply uneven task/axis performance; a benchmark aggregate lead does not imply broad manipulation competence.
The preprint notes that public baseline policies did not receive the wiki-derived task text supplied to the LLMs, limiting interpretation of leaderboard rank as a fully matched comparison.
The perturbation study uses selected small probes and traces; it does not isolate the cause of apparent corrections or establish general within-episode adaptation.

Across 42 RoboDojo simulation tasks and 2,100 trials, the authors report 22.48% average success and a score of 28.97, above the 40 public policies in their September 10 leaderboard snapshot. The result is uneven: Astra trails the top policy on precision, long-horizon and memory axes, while GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash perform much worse in the same reported interface. technical.claimed_result: Authors report 22.48% average success and 28.97 score for GPT-6 Astra over 2,100 simulated trials, above the 40 public policies in the cited snapshot. The comparison has a task-information mismatch and no independent reproduction was recovered.
technical.compute_or_cost: No comparable inference or robot-operation cost accounting was established in this review.
technical.demonstrated_result: The paper and its described protocol/results are publicly available in the arXiv preprint. The performance and hardware claims are not independently demonstrated by the research desk.
technical.implementation_status: Research evaluation reported in arXiv v1; no independent replication or production deployment assessment recovered.
technical.mechanism: A frozen vision-enabled language model selects world-frame end-effector targets through move_eef or give_up. Non-learned software validates targets, converts them to joint paths and executes them; simulation observations return achieved state/error to the model.
technical.novelty: Evaluates a general-purpose language model directly selecting executable manipulation targets at the full 42-task benchmark scale and compares its aggregate performance to a public policy board.
technical.regime: RoboDojo simulation: 42 tasks, 50 episodes/task for GPT-6 Astra and GPT-5.5, one seed and medium reasoning effort, with a default budget of 100 model calls/episode; public policies taken from the Sep 10, 2026 leaderboard snapshot. DeepSeek-Flash was tested at 10 episodes/task. Separate hardware diagnostic trials were incomplete.
technical.reproducibility: The full arXiv paper and linked author repository are accessible, but no independent reproduction, raw episode-data audit or maintainer confirmation was established.
technical.strongest_baseline: The paper compares against a Sep 10 public RoboDojo leaderboard snapshot and tests GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-Flash under the same reported action interface; wiki-derived task text was not supplied to public policy runs.

brief.title: A preprint reports GPT-6 Astra leading a simulated robot benchmark, with sharp control limits
brief.why_it_matters: If independently replicated under matched inputs, direct language-model action selection could change how semantic reasoning and low-level robot control are divided. The reported benchmark lead is limited by low absolute success, uneven capability, an input-information mismatch with public baselines and the authors' report of unsafe hardware actions.
